stem: A family member accompanies a client to an outpatient oncology clinic and reports a new cough and nasal congestion. Which action by clinic staff is appropriate?

options.A: Provide a facemask and ask the symptomatic family member not to enter patient-care areas, encouraging the person to wait outside or defer the visit.
options.B: Allow the family member into the treatment area without additional measures because only confirmed respiratory infections require precautions.
options.C: Permit entry as long as the family member avoids touching the client and remains at least one chair away from other people.
options.D: Delay screening until the family member develops fever because cough and congestion alone are not sufficient reasons for respiratory precautions.

rationale: CDC guidance for outpatient oncology settings applies respiratory-hygiene measures to patients, family members, caregivers, and visitors with respiratory symptoms such as cough or congestion. Symptomatic persons should be provided a facemask as appropriate, and accompanying persons with respiratory symptoms should not enter patient-care areas and should be encouraged to wait outside the facility. Precautions do not require a confirmed diagnosis or fever before action is taken.
educational_objective: Apply respiratory-infection screening and source-control measures to symptomatic visitors in outpatient oncology settings before they enter patient-care areas.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Basic Infection Control and Prevention Plan for Outpatient Oncology Settings; Preventing Transmission of Viral Respiratory Pathogens in Healthcare Settings
source_locator: Outpatient Oncology Plan, Section IV.C Respiratory Hygiene and Cough Etiquette — Identifying Persons with Potential Respiratory Infection and Masking and Separation of Persons with Respiratory Symptoms; Viral Respiratory Pathogens guidance — visitor recommendations
source_claim_supported: CDC applies respiratory-hygiene and source-control measures to symptomatic visitors and accompanying persons; outpatient oncology guidance states that accompanying persons with respiratory symptoms should not enter patient-care areas and should be encouraged to wait outside, with facemasks provided to symptomatic persons as appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — standard/transmission-based precautions, infection prevention, and environmental safety content
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory source control and visitor screening
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original rationale question into a concrete visitor-screening decision supported directly by CDC outpatient oncology and respiratory-pathogen guidance. Removed the overgeneralization that all oncology clients are immunosuppressed and the unsupported claim that visitor screening is uniformly an ongoing unit-wide policy independent of setting or risk. The final item tests symptoms-based source control before entry to patient-care areas.
audit_findings: Original item relied on a broad assertion about oncology clients being immunosuppressed rather than testing a specific infection-prevention action.
Fresh CDC review supports screening persons with cough/congestion, providing source-control measures, and excluding symptomatic accompanying persons from patient-care areas in outpatient oncology.
The final question does not require a confirmed respiratory diagnosis or fever before precautions are implemented.
Distractors represent common delay or minimization errors without introducing a second acceptable action.
Independent adversarial review found no ambiguity, cueing, unsupported universal policy claim, or unresolved source conflict.
